name: rgb-only-geometry-accuracy
authorization: User requested autonomous planning, execution and final selection; RGB evaluation must use pose-align; objective is accurate 3D reconstruction.

training.pose_recipe: Existing staged SIFT-reprojection BA + joint Gaussian optimization, fixed first training camera

geometry_evaluation.reference: Existing six-frame fixed-world TUM depth protocol
geometry_evaluation.confirmation: Positive mean primary gain across seeds42/43/44, wins at least2 seeds, mean gates pass; RGB aligned metrics reported without treating them as geometry truth

adaptive_combination: At most one combined candidate from separately beneficial initialization, initial opacity or MCMC noise settings and the best geometry loss; if no independent gains, keep the best single factor. Candidate definitions are fixed before full training.
data_isolation: MVS supervision uses all 37 original geometry TRAIN views, including 29 not selected into sharp99; no held-out timestamps. Fixed-camera geometry supervision every third RGB update cycles these views deterministically without changing RGB view RNG. Sensor depth is evaluation only. Validation/test RGB never enter initialization, priors or BA tracks. Previously inspected test frames are not a pristine holdout and are not used for selection.
mobile: No added foundation model runtime. Record desktop preprocessing/training time, peak allocation and Gaussian count. This study cannot certify mobile latency, temperature, energy or native training compatibility.
scope: Best among measured candidates on the current scene/protocol, not a claim of globally best 3D reconstruction or independent-scene generalization
pre_measurement_amendments: Timestamp inspection found only 8/37 geometry views in sharp99; use all original geometry TRAIN cameras rather than silently discarding 29 teachers.

Stage diagnosis found dense zero-step opacity-median surfaces much worse than sparse MVS point depths; add an opacity0.1 ablation to distinguish opacity/representation effects, without treating unequal-coverage stage errors as directly comparable accuracy.
